summary: Windows host-destruction wiper disguised as a utility library
details: The package advertises itself as a generic `Utility` but its sole exported function `sorgu(userId)` in index.js unconditionally invokes 26 sibling modules that perform destructive actions against the installer's Windows host. Observed behaviors include: recursive deletion of C:\Windows, Program Files, and Users; deletion of the SAM and SECURITY registry hives; zero-writing the master boot record of \\.\PhysicalDrive0; forced `shutdown /r /f /t 0`; `format C: /Q /Y`; killing winlogon/csrss/explorer/dwm via powershell/cmd child processes; disabling Windows recovery; hosts-file hijack; memory and fork bombs; and a full-screen screen-lock. The destructive modules are concealed under a 26-level single-letter directory tree (`public/a/b/c/.../z/a.js`..`z.js`), a nesting depth with no functional purpose that serves to hide the payload from casual review and path-based scanners. Any consumer that requires this package and calls its only public API destroys their Windows host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
